1. [blocking] math.js:2 — `add(a, b)` now returns `a - b`, breaking the function's contract with every caller. The export's name, signature, and any existing call sites all promise addition; `add(2, 3)` now yields `-1`. The change also silently breaks commutativity (`add(a, b) !== add(b, a)`), so callers using it for accumulation or identity (`add(x, 0) === x` holds, but `add(0, x)` now returns `-x`) get wrong results with no error. If subtraction was the intent, add a separate `subtract` export instead of repurposing `add`; otherwise revert. Existing tests asserting `add`'s behavior will fail and must be updated or the change reverted — the diff updates none.
